Top Festivals, Concerts & Plays You Won’t Want to Miss this Summer

by Vancouver Mom
July 24, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:17
Instaread

Metro Vancouver turns into a vibrant cultural playground each summer, filled with world-class concerts, multicultural festivals, and open-air theatre that draw crowds from all over BC and beyond. From free community celebrations to blockbuster Broadway musicals under the stars, there’s something for everyone in this dynamic and diverse region. Whether you’re a local planning your weekends or a visitor crafting the ultimate Vancouver itinerary, this ultimate 2026 guide to summer concerts, festivals and plays will keep your calendar full of unforgettable experiences. Get ready for live music, global flavours, family-friendly fun, and stunning performances all summer long!

Metro Vancouver Summer 2026 Festivals, Concerts and Plays

Theatre Under the Stars

Dates: July 3 – August 22, 2026
Location: Malkin Bowl, Stanley Park

Step into the magical world of musicals as Theatre Under the Stars lights up Stanley Park with Sister Act and The Little Mermaid. These energetic, family-friendly shows are set in the stunning Malkin Bowl, offering the ultimate picnic-and-a-show experience. A Vancouver summer staple for decades, TUTS promises music, laughter, and memorable nights under the stars.

Bard on the Beach

Dates: June 9 – September 19, 2026
Location: Vanier Park, Vancouver

Enjoy timeless stories of love, power, and wit under the setting sun. Bard on the Beach, Vancouver’s premier Shakespeare festival, returns to the beautiful waterfront setting of Vanier Park. This year’s line up is Macbeth, Antigone, and Goblin: Oedipus. With professional productions set against breathtaking views of the mountains and ocean, this summer tradition combines literary classics with natural beauty for a truly magical evening.

BC Halal Food Fest

Date: July 24-26, 2026
Location: Bill Reid Millennium Amphitheatre, Surrey, BC
Admission: Free
Time: July 24 (3pm-11pm), July 25 & 26 (11am-11pm)

Bring the whole crew to Bill Reid Millennium Amphitheatre in Surrey this weekend, July 24 to 26, for three days of halal eats, local shopping, and family fun. With over 50 food vendors and another 50-plus market stalls, plus carnival rides and live entertainment running all weekend, it’s an easy way to fill an afternoon (or three). Best part: it’s completely free to get in. 

Chiquitzin Kids Fiesta

Date: July 25, 2026
Location: Thompson Community Centre, Richmond
Cost: FREE

If you’re stuck on weekend plans, tomorrow’s the day to check out this free cultural mashup happening around Metro Vancouver, where Latin American and French traditions collide in the best way. Think live music, dance performances, theatre and storytelling, plus a magic show that’ll have the little ones’ jaws on the floor. There’s also arts and crafts, inflatables, face painting, and a photo booth for all those “proof we left the house” pics. My favourite part? Kids get a Chiquitzin passport to stamp along the way, with prizes and surprises hidden throughout the day. It’s the kind of low-effort, high-fun outing that fills a whole afternoon without you having to plan a thing.

Music with Marnie & Lightsaber show

Date: July 25, 2026
Location: KidsMarket on Granville Island

Music with Marnie — Free family show at 12:15pm right at Granville Island’s Kids Market. Marnie and her band bring the high-energy, up-on-your-feet tunes that turn any afternoon into a dance party, complete with puppets and costumed characters keeping the kids hooked from song one.

Lightsaber Show with Saber Guild Alderaan Temple — Two free shows at 12:00pm and 1:30pm bring epic lightsaber battles to life for Jedi, Padawans, and Sith of every age. Stick around after each performance for a meet-and-greet and photo op with the characters. May the Force be with you.

BC Pride Festival

Date: July 25, 2026
Location: Burnaby Civic Square, 6100 Willingdon Avenue, Burnaby, Admission: Free
Time: 3pm – 7pm

Head to Civic Square for Burnaby’s ninth annual Pride celebration, a free, family-friendly afternoon honouring the diversity of Burnaby’s 2SLGBTQIA+ community. Expect live music, drag, comedy, and educational booths, all set up to welcome families, kids, and allies alike. It’s a warm, community-first way to spend a summer afternoon and show your little ones what celebrating each other looks like.

 

Uptown Summer Live Series

Dates: June 27 – September 13, 2026
Location: Uptown New Westminister (Various Locations)
Cost: Free

Free, family-friendly, and running every Saturday and Sunday until September 13, Uptown Live turns New West into one big open-air stage with busker-style performances popping up across plazas, patios, and street corners all summer. No tickets, no cover, just wander the neighbourhood and let the music find you. Rain or shine, the show goes on.

Summer Light in English Bay

Date: July 31, 2026
Location: English Bay, Vancouver
Admission: Free
Time: The fireworks are expected to launch after dusk (around 10pm)

English Bay Beach lights up with a free, one-night fireworks show, no tickets needed. It falls on the closing weekend of Vancouver Pride and kicks off the BC Day long weekend, so expect big crowds and plan accordingly: walk, bike, or take transit if you can, since parking will be tight and several nearby lots will be closed. Grab a spot on the sand early, pack a blanket and snacks, and settle in for a night sky full of colour with the kids.

Summer in Langley City

Warmer, longer days mean live music under rainbow umbrellas, Shakespeare in the park, and juicy berries from the farmers market. Here’s what’s still on the calendar this summer, and it’s all free and family-friendly.

  • Langley Community Farmers Market — Fresh berries, food trucks, and live music from over 30 vendors, every Wednesday through August 26, 5:30–8:30pm at Douglas Park.
  • McBurney Plaza Summer Concert Series — Live music under a stunning aerial umbrella display, plus treats and giveaways. July 28 at McBurney Plaza.
  • Langley Pride Day — Drag bingo, live performances, and a 19+ concert with Disaster in a Dress and The Unbranded. August 8, noon–4pm (concert starts at 6pm), Creekside Hall.
  • Arts Alive Festival — Celebrating 30 years, with 200+ artists, live music, interactive installations, and artisan vendors filling downtown. August 15, 10am–5pm, Fraser Highway (between 204 and 206 streets).
  • Fork & Finger — A self-guided tasting trail through local restaurants, with feature dishes, live entertainment, and a chance to win $2,500 in Downtown Dollars. August 22, 11am–4pm, McBurney Plaza.
  • Heritage Classic Car Show — North America’s longest-running Jaguar-MG car show, with vintage motorcycles and restored classics rolling into Douglas Park. August 23, 10am–3:30pm.

Oval Community Day

Date: August 9 , 2026
Location: Richmond Olympic Oval
Admission: Free
Time: 10am-3pm

Free and family-friendly, this all-day celebration of sport and fitness takes over the Richmond Olympic Oval. Kids can tackle inflatable obstacle courses (including a 90-foot challenge and a bungee run), try sports like fencing, foosball, and wheelchair basketball, and get their face painted between snacks from Kona Ice and Tap & Snack’s BBQ. There’s live music, circus acts, and gymnastics showcases throughout the day, plus prize giveaways and self-guided tours of the Olympic Experience if you need a break from the sun.

PNE Summer Night Concerts: Summer’s Hottest Stage

Dates: August 22 – September 7, 2025
Location: Pacific National Exhibition (PNE), Vancouver

The PNE Fair’s most anticipated tradition returns, and this year it’s got a serious upgrade: the brand new Freedom Mobile Arch. This purpose built amphitheatre brings better sightlines and top tier acoustics, so whether you’re bringing the whole family or sneaking out for a date night, every seat feels like a good one. The lineup spans rock, pop, hip hop, alternative, and orchestral acts, so there’s genuinely something for every taste in the house. Tickets start at $49 plus fees and include full access to the PNE Fair, meaning your concert night doubles as a trip to the midway, the animal barns, and all the fair food you can handle.d-of-summer event paired with mini donuts and midway fun.

Plan Your Ultimate Summer in Vancouver

Whether you’re looking for family-friendly fun, live music by the ocean, multicultural feasts, or open-air theatre, Metro Vancouver’s summer events calendar for 2026 is bursting with opportunity. From Surrey to Fort Langley and the heart of downtown Vancouver, there’s something happening every weekend. Bookmark this list, grab your friends or your little ones, and get ready for a summer full of celebration, culture, and unforgettable memories.
